title: Late-Night Canadian Poutine
description: A yeasty, cheese-pull take on classic Canadian poutine, perfect for midnight cravings.
instructions: In a small bowl, combine fast action yeast and warm water. Let sit for 5 minutes, until frothy.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour and sugar. Add yeast mixture and mix until a sticky dough forms.
Knead the dough on a floured surface for 5 minutes, until smooth.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let rise in a warm place for 30-40 minutes, until doubled in size.
Roll out the dough to a 1/4-inch thickness. Place on a baking sheet and bake for 12-15 minutes, until golden brown.
In a separate pan, cook score-fat bacon slices over medium-high heat, until crispy. Drain on paper towels.
In a greased 9x13-inch baking dish, layer cooked bacon, half the shredded Gruy5re, and half the baked dough. Repeat the layers.
Drizzle with melted butter and sprinkle remaining Gruy5re on top.
Bake in the preheated oven for an additional 5-7 minutes, until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Remove from oven and sprinkle with chopped chives. Let cool for a few minutes before serving.
Slice into squares and serve immediately.
